newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota livestock losses drastically high.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota livestock losses drastically high.

text.p: North Dakota cattle and calf losses were said to be running drastically above average, the state's agricultural statistics service said on Monday in its monthly crop report.

Improved weather conditions during the week, which ended Sunday, allowed North Dakota ranchers to assess losses from the intense April 4-6 blizzard. In all, North Dakota cattle and calf death loss was assessed at 100 percent above normal compared to 60 percent reported on April 6.
"Cattle and calf losses, particularly in the southern half of the state, may be unprecedented," the report said.

Statewide cattle conditions on April 13 were rated four percent very poor, 15 poor, 39 fair, 40 good and two percent excellent. Calves were rated four percent very poor, 16 poor, 36 fair, 41 good and three excellent.
Meanwhile, continued problems with flooding pushed back planting activity. The statewide average starting date for fieldwork is expected to be May 2, well behind average.
No plantings were reported as of April 13, same as last year. The five-year average shows two percent of spring wheat and oats, one percent of barley and no durum acres planted.
